newsitem.title: UK: JGBs best performer in week, U.S. suffers - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: JGBs best performer in week, U.S. suffers - Salomon.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) turned in the top performance among major bond markets in the latest weak while U.S. Treasuries were the worst investment, according to data from Salomon Brothers on Friday.
JGBs, inspired by a Bank of Japan report showing weak corporate sentiment, returned 0.96 percent in yen terms as the market took the view an interest rate increase in Japan may not be so imminent.
Finnish bonds were a distant second, returning 0.51 percent in the local currency, in what was a mixed week for bond markets overall.
Seven of the 16 major markets in Salomon's world government bond index turned in losses in local currency terms, and the index itself was down 0.16 percent in the week ended Thursday.
U.S. Treasuries lost investors 0.93 percent in the week. In the year so far, they are the only major market in negative territory, with a 1.42 percent loss.
High-yielders Italy, Spain and Sweden remain the top performers in the year to date with returns of 11.16, 10.45 and 8.03 percent respectively.
But the high-yielders were less than impressive during the latest week. Italy squeaked out a 0.13 percent return in lira terms and Spain managed 0.07 percent, while Swedish bonds lost 0.38 percent.

Analysts said nagging worries about European budgets in the coming months, and the problems they posed in terms of European economic and monetary union (EMU), were weighing on peripheral bond markets in Europe. All the dollar bloc markets suffered in the week in their local currencies, with Canada following the U.S. lead by losing 0.53 percent. Australian bonds had a negative return of 0.42 percent and New Zealand, which is outside the main Salomon index, lost 0.10 percent.
In U.S. dollar terms, Finland took top honours, returning 1.66 percent. It was followed closely by Switzerland with 1.52 percent and Austria with 1.51.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
